A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PURE study and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–D. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison of the equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original PRM evaluations, reinforcement fine-tuning results, training analyses, and temperature ablations in Sections 4–5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, including PURE results in Tables 1–5 and training curves and reward-hacking examples in Figures 1–8.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 retain the same min-form credit assignment, reward transformation, token-level reward assignment, and RLOO advantage estimator.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same PRM800K and MATH training data, GSM8K/MATH best-of-N evaluation, five reasoning benchmarks, and ProcessBench/PRMBench coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches throughout Tables 1–4 and Section 5.3, including Eurus-2-7B-PRIME, SimpleRL-Zoo, Qwen2.5-7B-DPO-Zero, and the advantage-estimator comparisons.

E3.justification: The model configurations, data allocation, training budgets, hyperparameters, greedy pass@1 evaluation, best-checkpoint selection, and Appendix D temperature-ablation protocol are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both versions contain identical reward-hacking cases, training-collapse analysis, advantage-estimator comparisons, and transform-temperature ablation in Section 5 and Appendices C–D.

E5.justification: No repeated-run counts, seed information, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests are added or revised. Tables and training curves retain the same reporting practices.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and plotted findings match, including Table 2's 82.5% AMC23 accuracy and 53.3% average for Qwen2.5-Math-7B with PURE-PRM+VR. Appendix benchmark and ablation results are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(10), the min-form definitions, reward-transformation limiting argument, and advantage derivations are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about reward hacking, min-form credit assignment, learning efficiency, auxiliary verifiable rewards, and training collapse.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations concerning causal PRMs, short or empty responses, repetitive pseudo-positive samples, and potential generative PRMs remain unchanged.

D1.justification: PRM training details, RL hyperparameters, metric definitions, step-separation instructions, and code/model access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Li et al. (2025), From system 1 to system 2: A survey of reasoning large language models, to the introduction's existing statement about sparse-reward inefficiency and adds its bibliography entry. Research positioning otherwise remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The introductory citation text and first-page arXiv version/date stamp change. The prose, terminology, section organization, and appendix structure otherwise remain identical.

P2.justification: The added bibliography entry reflows references across pages 12–14. All eight figures and five tables retain identical displays, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 adds one survey citation to an already cited background statement, with associated bibliography reflow and a version-stamp update. Methods, mathematical reasoning, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information are unchanged, so the revision does not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
